title: Zeraki Review 2026: Is It Right for Your Kenyan School?
h1: Zeraki Review 2026: Is It Right for Your Kenyan School?
description: A balanced Zeraki review for Kenyan schools — what it does best, where it falls short on M-Pesa and WhatsApp, who it suits, and the strongest alternative.
author: SQUL Team
intro: This is a fair, plainly-written **Zeraki review** for Kenyan schools: what it is genuinely good at, where it leaves gaps, who it suits, and what to pick instead if your priorities are different. It sits alongside our bigger picture, the [best school management software in Kenya](/blog/best-school-management-software-kenya).

We are a competing vendor, so hold us to a higher standard: we have written what Zeraki gets right, not only what suits us. Judge each claim against your own school, and verify current details with Zeraki directly.
quickAnswer: Editor's note: this review describes features and positioning at a high level from public information, and competitor details change over time. Verify current capabilities and pricing with Zeraki before deciding. Last reviewed September 2026.

blocks.text: Zeraki is one of the most recognisable education-technology names in Kenya. It is best known among secondary schools, and its reputation rests largely on **exam analytics and academic reporting** — the work of turning marks into insight a head teacher can act on. It also offers SMS-based communication, which is the channel many Kenyan schools already use.

items: **Exam analytics.** Performance analysis and reporting are its strongest suit, and schools that compete on results value this.
**Brand trust.** Parents, staff and boards often already know the name, which lowers the explanation cost of adopting it.
**Secondary-school focus.** Its footprint is strong in secondary schools, where exam reporting matters most.
**SMS communication.** It reaches parents over SMS, which works for guardians who are not on WhatsApp.

blocks.caption: Zeraki scorecard for a Kenyan school (indicative).

sections.heading: Where it falls short for many schools

blocks.text: Zeraki is a good fit for some schools and a poorer fit for others. The gaps schools most often raise are operational:

items: **Fees.** Automatic, Daraja-based M-Pesa reconciliation is not what Zeraki is centred on, so bursars can still end up matching payments by hand.
**WhatsApp.** SMS-only messaging misses parents who live in WhatsApp, and reminders are less effective as a result.
**One system.** If you also need live fee balances and two-channel messaging, you may end up adding another tool.
**Time to value.** Getting to "we are collecting fees in it" can take longer than a school would like.

blocks.title: Verify, don't assume
blocks.text: Vendors ship new features constantly. If fees or WhatsApp matter to you, ask Zeraki to show those exact workflows in a live demo before you rule it in or out.

items: Schools whose **top priority is exam analytics and reporting**.
Schools that are **already trained on it** and for whom switching is not worth it.
Schools whose **fee reconciliation and parent messaging** are already handled acceptably elsewhere.

sections.heading: The strongest alternative if fees and WhatsApp matter

blocks.text: If your review of Zeraki leaves you wanting more on fees and parent communication, the natural alternative is **SQUL**, which was built around exactly those two jobs.

items: **Automatic M-Pesa reconciliation (Daraja)** — Paybill and till payments matched to the right learner automatically.
**WhatsApp and SMS** — reminders, absence alerts and exam notices on both channels from one place.
**CBC and 8-4-4 report cards**, plus timetables, duty rosters, and same-day attendance alerts.
**Free term to start**, then per-term pricing, and live in about two weeks.

blocks.caption: The gap SQUL closes: reaching parents on WhatsApp and SMS, and closing the loop with a receipt.

blocks.text: Compare the two directly in [SQUL vs Zeraki](/blog/squl-vs-zeraki), or see the broader [Zeraki alternatives](/blog/zeraki-alternatives-kenya) list.

Zeraki is a credible, well-known platform and a genuinely good choice for schools whose priority is exam analytics. For schools whose daily pain is **obtaining and reconciling fees and reaching parents**, it is not the strongest fit, and **SQUL** is the better alternative — stronger on automatic M-Pesa and WhatsApp plus SMS, with CBC reports included. Decide on your own priorities, and demand a live demo of the workflows you actually run.

faqs.question: Is Zeraki a good school management system?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right school. Zeraki is strong on exam analytics and reporting and is well known in Kenyan secondary schools. It is a weaker fit if automatic M-Pesa reconciliation and WhatsApp parent messaging are your priorities.

faqs.question: What are the downsides of Zeraki?
faqs.answer: Schools most often note that automatic M-Pesa reconciliation and WhatsApp messaging are not its focus, so fee handling and parent communication can need extra tools. Verify current capabilities with the vendor.

faqs.question: Does Zeraki handle school fees and M-Pesa?
faqs.answer: It offers school-fees features, but automatic Daraja-based reconciliation is not its core focus. Confirm the exact M-Pesa workflow in a demo before relying on it.

faqs.question: What is the best alternative to Zeraki?
faqs.answer: If fees and parent communication are your priority, SQUL is the strongest alternative — automatic M-Pesa reconciliation and WhatsApp plus SMS, with CBC report cards, for a free term to start.

faqs.question: Is Zeraki good for primary schools?
faqs.answer: Zeraki is best known in secondary schools. Primary and CBC-focused schools should compare options that centre on CBC assessment and fee collection, such as SQUL.

faqs.question: Should I switch from Zeraki?
faqs.answer: Switch if your biggest problems are fee reconciliation and reaching parents on WhatsApp. Stay if exam analytics is your priority and is working well for you.
